etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin praescrībere, from prae- (“before, in front”) and scrībere (“to write”).

definitions.definition: (medicine) To order (a drug or medical device) for use by a particular patient (under licensed authority).
To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1606, William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of King Lear”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene i]:

1665 (first performance), John Dryden, The Indian Emperour, or, The Conquest of Mexico by the Spaniards. […], London:  […]  J[ohn] M[acock] for H[enry] Herringman […], published 1667, →OCLC, Act I, scene ii, page 5:
quote.text: VVhen Parents loves are order'd by a Son, / Let ſtreams preſcribe their fountains vvhere to run.

definitions.definition: (law) To develop or assert a right; to make a claim (by prescription).

quote.citation: 1753, Andrew McDouall, An Institute of the Laws of Scotland in Civil Rights  […] , volume 3, Table of Contents, page 86:
quote.text: Most probable that one presentation and 40 years possession thereafter, is sufficient to prescribe a right of patronage.

quote.text: […]  held, in a question with a party who had acquired right from the commissioners of the forfeited estates to the estate of the forfeited superior, as it stood in his person, that the crown charter of the vassal was a valid title on which to prescribe a right to the coal  […]
